page: Amazon Web Services m5d.8xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8175M processor operating at 3.1 GHz with x86_64 architecture. The server provides 32 vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU features 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 33 MB L3 cache, supporting instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512, and AES. Memory capacity totals 128.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU.

Storage and networking configurations feature 1200 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a baseline network throughput of 10 Gbps. No dedicated GPUs are included with this instance type. In benchmark testing, the Intel Xeon 8175M delivers average multi-threaded execution metrics, registering 27,102.44 on stress-ng multi-core and 9,429.0 on Geekbench multi-core. Single-threaded performance lands in the lower tier, scoring 1,033.0 in Geekbench single-core and 1,285.98 in stress-ng single-core. Memory subsystem testing shows uncached large-block read bandwidth of 97.72 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 45.58 GB/sec.

System-level workloads demonstrate competitive middle-tier throughput, recording 25.68 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 20.47 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks. In machine learning inference, smaller 135M parameter models execute at 1,074.66 prompt tokens per second and 113.79 text generation tokens per second, but performance degrades on larger language models due to the absence of dedicated GPU accelerators. The local NVMe storage provides high-throughput scratch space without incurring detached volume network latency.

The instance delivers qualitative cost efficiency for multi-threaded applications that require direct fast storage paired with balanced memory capacity. While single-thread-constrained tasks may experience performance limitations compared to newer processor architectures, m5d.8xlarge fits distributed relational databases, in-memory caches, backend API clusters, data ingestion pipelines, and build environments needing low-latency local NVMe scratch disk.
description: Amazon Web Services m5d.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8175M processor, built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It provides 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, 128 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, and 1200 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. The network interface delivers a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps. Benchmark results demonstrate modest single-thread metrics alongside balanced multi-threaded compute, scoring 27,102.44 on stress-ng multi-core and 9,429.0 on Geekbench multi-core. Memory bandwidth reaches 97.72 GB/sec for uncached reads, while Redis achieves 25.68 million operations per second. Lacking hardware acceleration, large-model AI generation remains constrained. The integrated high-speed NVMe storage and balanced 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio position this server well for relational databases, caching layers, batch ETL processing, and web serving environments requiring fast local disk access.
